findings.title: CAUTION claims the operator fails without the rolling-updates feature, but the scope is wrong
findings.body: The new CAUTION block in the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' section states unconditionally: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This is contradicted by this PR's own tests (UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment): when no update strategy is set (the default case, which the same page documents as a valid configuration), the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is NOT enabled and the operator is expected to work (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount run with null strategy and no feature). A reader will conclude that every deployment — or at least any deployment using the default update behavior — must enable the feature or the operator breaks, which is not the case per the tests. The caution should be scoped to explicitly setting `spec.update.strategy` (e.g. `Recreate`), matching what the tests and the rest of the section actually require.

findings.title: New and changed exit codes (3 and 4) are never asserted in tests
findings.body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces exit code 4 for the feature-disabled case, and the documentation explicitly promises these exit codes to scripting/CI consumers ('they should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). Yet no test asserts them: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr message, not exit code 4; testWrongVersions asserts only the error message, not exit code 3; testCompatible only asserts exit code 0 for the metadata command, not for the check command. A regression in any of these exit codes (e.g. accidentally reusing 4, or returning the picocli default 1) would pass the entire suite while breaking the documented contract that automation depends on.

findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changes from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for feature-disabled
findings.body: The check command previously exited with 4 when a recreate upgrade was required; it now exits with 3, and 4 is repurposed to mean 'the rolling-updates feature is disabled'. While this aligns the code with the existing documentation (which already documented 3 for recreate), any user who scripted against the actually-shipped behavior will now see exit code 4 (previously 'recreate needed') only when the feature is disabled, and exit code 3 where they expected 4 — i.e. existing pipelines that branch on these codes will misclassify results. Since both values ultimately mean 'do not do a rolling upgrade' the practical impact is limited, but the release notes / upgrade docs should call out this behavioral change for early adopters of the preview command.
